brief:
Shehab Wire examined the gap between international recognition of Palestinian statehood and on-the-ground reality, nearly four decades after the 1988 declaration. The analysis highlighted the disconnect between diplomatic acknowledgment and Palestinian sovereignty, as Israeli occupation and settlement expansion persist across the territories.

Palestinians lack control over land, border crossings, and natural resources despite widespread international recognition of their state. The declared state remains largely symbolic, without the functional sovereignty needed to exercise governing power over territory and resources.

title: Palestinian statehood remains unrealized 38 years after declaration
